title: Making a choice
subtitle: Evidence accumulating to a threshold
question: What happens when you decide between two options?
teaser: Watch a choice get made as evidence piles up and crosses a line.
intro: A decision does not happen in an instant. Evidence for each option builds up over time, and the choice happens when one of them crosses a line. Where that line sits decides whether you are fast and careless or slow and careful — and it moves.

events.title: Both options are represented
events.explanation: Both options get recognised. At this point neither is preferred — they just both exist.

events.title: Each is assigned a value
events.explanation: Each one gets a worth, based on your current state. They end up on the same scale, which is the only reason they can be compared at all.
events.science: Value signals here are state-dependent: the same option is valued differently when you are hungry, tired, or have just had one.

events.title: Context modifies the values
events.explanation: The situation adjusts those numbers. Who you are with, what you decided this morning, what you are trying to do generally.

events.title: Evidence accumulates
events.explanation: The difference between the options gets added up over time. Activity ramps in a way that tracks that adding-up.
events.science: Ramping activity whose slope predicts both the choice and the reaction time is one of the most reproducible findings in decision neuroscience.

events.title: The accumulation is noisy
events.explanation: The adding-up is messy. When the options are close, the mess decides — which is why you can choose differently on identical occasions.

events.title: Urgency rises
events.explanation: As time passes, the line gets lower. Waiting costs something, so the system gradually becomes easier to satisfy.
events.science: Collapsing-bound models capture the fact that people eventually commit even when evidence remains ambiguous. Pure fixed-threshold models do not.

events.title: The threshold is crossed
events.explanation: One option crosses the line. The decision happens here — not when you became aware of it.

events.title: The action is released
events.explanation: The chosen action gets released and the other gets held back. Holding back is as much of the work as choosing.

events.title: You become aware of having decided
events.explanation: You become aware of having decided. The order is measurable and reliable, and it is uncomfortable.
events.science: That preparatory activity precedes reported awareness of deciding is well established. What this implies about agency is contested, and we take no position on it.

events.title: The outcome updates the values
events.explanation: Whatever happens next changes what these options are worth. The next identical choice will not be worked out identically.

causalChain.label: Urgency lowers the bar

causalChain.detail: Awareness of having decided comes afterwards.

science.text: Neural activity in parietal and frontal regions ramps during decisions in a way that predicts both the choice and the time taken.
Orbitofrontal value signals are state-dependent and are expressed on a comparable scale across different kinds of options.
Preparatory motor activity precedes a person's reported awareness of having decided to act.
Choices between closely matched options are variable across repetitions of the same situation.
We draw a single accumulator with one threshold. Real decisions appear to involve multiple competing accumulators with mutual inhibition.
The accumulation trace in the panel is produced by a small random-walk model written for this page, not by a model of neural populations.
That preparation precedes reported awareness is a measurement. What it means for free will is a philosophical dispute, and this project does not resolve it or take a side.

references.label: Drift-diffusion models
references.note: A framework describing decisions as noisy accumulation of evidence to a threshold, fitting both choices and reaction-time distributions.

references.label: Common currency value coding
references.note: Evidence that orbitofrontal cortex represents value on a scale that permits comparison across option types.

references.label: Collapsing bounds
references.note: Models in which the decision threshold decreases over time, accounting for commitment under persistent ambiguity.

references.label: Readiness potentials
references.note: Measurements showing motor preparation preceding reported awareness of a decision to move.

readouts.label: Decision speed
readouts.note: How quickly the model reaches a decision.

readouts.label: Choice consistency
readouts.note: How reliably it makes the same choice when the situation repeats.

readouts.label: Effective threshold
readouts.note: How much evidence it wants before committing. Higher means slower and more careful.

outcome.headline: Deciding
outcome.body: Two options were given a worth on the same scale, the difference between them was added up messily over time, impatience gradually lowered the bar, and the choice happened when one crossed it.
outcome.insight: The decision was made before you knew about it, and if the options had been closer, noise would have picked for you. Your sense of having weighed it up is a report about something you did not watch.
